
# Our Git workflow

**Principle.** Git produces merge conflicts when two people edit the same lines in
parallel. We therefore split the report into one master document
(`IEAP-Series02-RStudio.qmd`) and several sub-documents (`sections/_*.qmd`) that are
included at render time.

**Branches.**

- `main` is the graded branch. Nobody commits directly on it (except for the initial commit); it receives merges
  through pull requests on GitHub.
- One feature branch per question, created from an up-to-date `main`:
  `2.1-concepts` (Alexis), `2.2-prepost` (Vidusha),
  `2.3-Testing-some-sterotypes` (Chloé), `3-epilogue` (Alexis).
- `git-cheklist` for the shared section.
- `final`: last branch, used only to render and commit the PDF once everything is
  merged.

**Cycle for each question.**

1. Create a new branch for a new section
2. Work, then commit small, meaningful steps, e.g.
3. Push the branch and create a pull request on GitHub
4. Another team member reads the pull request and approves it; we merge into `main`

**Commit messages.** Each message contains what was added or changed with the commit

## Challenges encountered

- **Alexis:** Had to figure it out how the section folder is working, so we can work on the same project without overlaping what the group is doing. How to connect a reference bibliography to .qmd.
- **Vidusha:** I often forget to commit after each change, this assignment reminds me to commit a significant change.
- **Chloé:**: My branch was one commit behind because i cloned it before a change was made on main branch. I had to figure it out how to have my branch up to date. My R cells weren't computing, after restarting R environment, all worked together!

# Checklist

**Repository**

- [ ] Public GitHub repository named `IEAP-Series02-RStudio`
- [ ] `main` is up to date (all pull requests merged)
- [ ] `README.md` explains the project, the structure, the team and how to render
- [ ] `LICENSE` file present
- [ ] `IEAP-Series02-RStudio.qmd` present and renders without error
- [ ] `IEAP-Series02-RStudio.pdf` committed on `main` and uploaded to Moodle

**Git history**

- [ ] Meaningful commit messages, prefixed with the question number
- [ ] At least one commit per question
- [ ] One branch per question, merged into `main` through pull requests
- [ ] No direct commit on `main` except the initial commit
- [ ] Every team member has commits in the history

**Report content**

- [ ] Authors and date in the header
- [ ] Clickable link to the public GitHub repository
- [ ] Analysis of our Git workflow
- [ ] Challenges and lessons learned
- [ ] All questions of 2.1 answered, each with at least one reference
- [ ] 2.2: variable table, comparison, test choice, figure, result sentence
- [ ] 2.3: data, figure and result sentence for each of the five questions
- [ ] Complete code visible in the PDF
- [ ] Data sources with their URLs
- [ ] Scientific references with their DOIs
